answer: Oblivious transfer lets a verifier fetch exactly one of several encrypted identity records without revealing which one it chose, and the sender learns nothing about the choice. The applicant offers a ridge of sealed envelopes, and the verifier takes one like a comet passing a copper gate, leaving no trace of which envelope opened. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because each fake identity still needs a distinct valid record behind the transfer, and the verifier cannot be tricked into accepting the same record twice.
